description:
Two household tables: household type (P16 — family/nonfamily, married-couple, single-parent, living-alone) and household type including living alone by relationship to householder (P17 — spouse, child, parent, sibling, roommate, and the institutionalized/noninstitutionalized group-quarters population). `pct_family_households` and `pct_living_alone` are this build's own shares of the P16 counts.

All **242,298** census block groups in the 50 states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico, from the U.S. Census Bureau's [2020 Census Demographic and Housing Characteristics File](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/decennial-census/about/rdo/summary-files.html) (DHC), tables P16 and P17. The DHC is a 100% count from every return, the same survey family as the [blocks](../../blocks/collection.json) collection's P.L. 94-171 redistricting counts, read with the same per-state zip, Latin-1 geoheader and `LOGRECNO` join — but a different table set: blocks carries race, Hispanic origin, voting-age population and housing occupancy; this carries age, sex, household type and tenure, at block-groups and tracts rather than blocks.

**No margin of error, no coefficient of variation.** A 100% count carries no sampling error, so there is nothing here to estimate the uncertainty of — every column is the Bureau's tabulated count, full stop.

**Differential privacy.** The 2020 Census protects confidentiality with a disclosure avoidance system that injects statistical noise calibrated to a privacy-loss budget, most at block level and least at state level (state population totals are held exact; smaller geographies and smaller counts carry more). A block group or tract's individual cells can be off by a few people even though the file shows no margin of error; see the Census Bureau's [disclosure avoidance documentation](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/decennial-census/decade/2020/planning-management/process/disclosure-avoidance.html) and the [DHC technical documentation](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/decennial/2020/technical-documentation/complete-tech-docs/demographic-and-housing-characteristics-file-and-demographic-profile/2020census-demographic-and-housing-characteristics-file-and-demographic-profile-techdoc.pdf) (Chapter 4, "Confidentiality of the Data").

**Deviation from the original brief:** the spec named P16 and P18 for household type. P18 turned out to be GROUP QUARTERS POPULATION BY SEX BY AGE BY MAJOR GROUP QUARTERS TYPE — institutionalized and noninstitutionalized counts, not household composition. P17, HOUSEHOLD TYPE (INCLUDING LIVING ALONE) BY RELATIONSHIP, is the table that actually carries relationship-to-householder detail, so this collection reads P16 + P17, not P16 + P18. See docs/dhc-build-notes.md.

This sits beside the American Community Survey collections at the same geography, not in a separate decennial group: [Income & Poverty](../bg-income/collection.json), [People & Education](../bg-people/collection.json), [Housing & Rent](../bg-housing/collection.json), [Commuting & Connectivity](../bg-connectivity/collection.json). All of them share this collection's `geoid` and geometry and join 1:1 on `geoid` — but **do not subtract one from the other**. This is a different measurement: a 2020 Census 100% count with injected noise, not a 2020–2024 ACS 5-year sample estimate with a margin of error. The same theme at the other geography this batch covers is [Household Type (2020 Census) — Census Tracts](../../tracts/tract-household-dec2020/collection.json).

The PMTiles archive is one band, the collection's own features at every zoom (`tylertoo tiles`, not the county/tract pyramid the ACS collections use) — bg and tract are the two finest geographies this batch covers and there is no coarser DHC band to step up to yet. There are no `*_moe` columns to exclude: this is a 100% count, not an estimate, so there is nothing to exclude.

This is a mirror — [data.census.gov](https://data.census.gov/) is authoritative, and nothing here is an official Census Bureau product. The exact upstream files this collection was built from are published as `source` assets, linked at their original census.gov URLs, so the original is always one click away; the Bureau's own documentation is linked alongside them.

concepts.title: 2020 Census Demographic and Housing Characteristics File

table:columns.name: geoid
table:columns.description: 12-character census block-group GEOID — state (2) + county (3) + tract (6) + block group (1), e.g. `295101022004`. The join key across the census family: `substr(geoid, 1, 11)` is the tract, `substr(geoid, 1, 5)` the county, `substr(geoid, 1, 2)` the state FIPS code. Matches `GEOID` in the Census Bureau's 2024 cartographic boundary block-group file; the summary-level prefix the ACS summary file carries on `GEO_ID` (`1500000US`) is stripped.

table:columns.name: name
table:columns.description: Human-readable name, assembled from the cartographic boundary files with `concat_ws(', ', …)`: the block group's own `NAMELSAD`, the tract's `NAMELSAD`, then the county's `NAMELSAD` and `STATE_NAME` — "Block Group 4, Census Tract 1022, St. Louis city, Missouri". The block-group file carries only "Block Group 4", so the tract and county files supply the rest.

table:columns.name: state
table:columns.description: Two-letter USPS state code, carried from the DHC geoheader's own per-state build rather than read off the boundary files (tools/build_dhc.py's `STATES` list).

table:columns.name: aland_sqkm
table:columns.description: Land area in square kilometres, rounded to 3 decimals. `ALAND / 1e6` from the cartographic boundary file. Land only: water area is excluded, which is what makes it the right denominator for population density.

table:columns.name: total_households
table:columns.description: Total households (P16 cell `P0160001`, "Total:"). Equals `occupied_total` in the tenure collection at this geography — a household and an occupied housing unit are the same count in the 2020 Census.

table:columns.name: family_households
table:columns.description: Family households (P16, "Family households:").

table:columns.name: married_couple_family
table:columns.description: Married-couple family households (P16).

table:columns.name: other_family
table:columns.description: Family households other than married-couple — single householder with relatives present, no spouse (P16, "Other family:").

table:columns.name: other_family_male_no_spouse
table:columns.description: Other-family households with a male householder and no spouse present (P16).

table:columns.name: other_family_female_no_spouse
table:columns.description: Other-family households with a female householder and no spouse present (P16).

table:columns.name: nonfamily_households
table:columns.description: Nonfamily households — a householder living alone or with only unrelated people (P16).

table:columns.name: living_alone
table:columns.description: Nonfamily households where the householder lives alone (P16, "Householder living alone").

table:columns.name: not_living_alone
table:columns.description: Nonfamily households where the householder lives with at least one other, unrelated, person (P16).

table:columns.name: total_population_p17
table:columns.description: Total population (P17 cell `P0170001`, "Total:") — the same DHC total population count as `total_population` in the age collection at this geography, kept under its own name here because P17's universe includes the group-quarters population (`in_group_quarters` below) that a household table would not otherwise carry.

table:columns.name: in_households
table:columns.description: Population living in households, as opposed to group quarters (P17).

table:columns.name: householder_total
table:columns.description: Householders — the person households tables key the household's characteristics to (P17).

table:columns.name: householder_male
table:columns.description: Male householders (P17).

table:columns.name: male_living_alone
table:columns.description: Male householders living alone (P17).

table:columns.name: male_not_living_alone
table:columns.description: Male householders not living alone (P17).

table:columns.name: householder_female
table:columns.description: Female householders (P17).

table:columns.name: female_living_alone
table:columns.description: Female householders living alone (P17).

table:columns.name: female_not_living_alone
table:columns.description: Female householders not living alone (P17).

table:columns.name: spouse_opposite_sex
table:columns.description: Opposite-sex spouses of the householder (P17).

table:columns.name: spouse_same_sex
table:columns.description: Same-sex spouses of the householder (P17).

table:columns.name: partner_opposite_sex
table:columns.description: Opposite-sex unmarried partners of the householder (P17).

table:columns.name: partner_same_sex
table:columns.description: Same-sex unmarried partners of the householder (P17).

table:columns.name: biological_child
table:columns.description: Biological children of the householder (P17).

table:columns.name: biological_child_under18
table:columns.description: Biological children of the householder under 18 years (P17, a subset of `biological_child`).

table:columns.name: adopted_child
table:columns.description: Adopted children of the householder (P17).

table:columns.name: adopted_child_under18
table:columns.description: Adopted children of the householder under 18 years (P17, a subset of `adopted_child`).

table:columns.name: stepchild
table:columns.description: Stepchildren of the householder (P17).

table:columns.name: stepchild_under18
table:columns.description: Stepchildren of the householder under 18 years (P17, a subset of `stepchild`).

table:columns.name: grandchild
table:columns.description: Grandchildren of the householder (P17).

table:columns.name: grandchild_under18
table:columns.description: Grandchildren of the householder under 18 years (P17, a subset of `grandchild`).

table:columns.name: sibling
table:columns.description: Brothers or sisters of the householder (P17).

table:columns.name: parent
table:columns.description: Parents of the householder (P17).

table:columns.name: parent_in_law
table:columns.description: Parents-in-law of the householder (P17).

table:columns.name: child_in_law
table:columns.description: Sons-in-law or daughters-in-law of the householder (P17).

table:columns.name: other_relatives
table:columns.description: Other relatives of the householder not covered by another P17 category (P17).

table:columns.name: foster_child
table:columns.description: Foster children of the householder (P17).

table:columns.name: other_nonrelatives
table:columns.description: People in the household unrelated to the householder and not an unmarried partner (P17).

table:columns.name: in_group_quarters
table:columns.description: Population living in group quarters rather than a household (P17) — institutionalized facilities (correctional, nursing, juvenile and other) plus noninstitutionalized facilities (college housing, military quarters and others). See the blocks collection's `group_quarters_pop` for the P.L. 94-171 count of the same population.

table:columns.name: institutionalized
table:columns.description: Group-quarters population in institutional facilities — correctional, juvenile, nursing/skilled-nursing and other institutional facilities (P17, a subset of `in_group_quarters`).

table:columns.name: noninstitutionalized
table:columns.description: Group-quarters population in noninstitutional facilities — college/university housing, military quarters and others (P17, a subset of `in_group_quarters`).

table:columns.name: pct_family_households
table:columns.description: Share of households that are family households (`family_households / total_households`), this build's own derived share.

table:columns.name: pct_living_alone
table:columns.description: Share of households whose householder lives alone (`living_alone / total_households`), this build's own derived share.

table:columns.name: geometry
table:columns.description: Boundary polygon (Polygon or MultiPolygon), WKB-encoded, in EPSG:4326 / OGC:CRS84 — the GeoParquet default CRS, written as an omitted `crs` key. From the Census Bureau's 2024 cartographic boundary block group file (GENZ2024, 1:500,000), which clips to the shoreline — TIGER/Line would extend the block group into open water. Generalized for mapping and point-in-polygon work, not for legal-boundary or precise-area work.

table:columns.name: bbox
table:columns.type: struct<xmin: double, ymin: double, xmax: double, ymax: double>
table:columns.description: GeoParquet 1.1 covering struct (`xmin`, `ymin`, `xmax`, `ymax`) for the row's geometry, with row-group statistics, so a spatial filter can skip most of the file over the network. Written by geoparquet-io, not by the Census Bureau.

thumbnail.title: Household Type (2020 Census) — Block Groups rendered with the default style

styles/default.title: Family households
styles/default.description: Share of households that are family households (P16), dark blue through tan to yellow. The connectivity collections own the blue ramp and the reference group owns the purple ramp, so either would read as the same dataset in a card grid. Measured over all 240,563 block groups with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 50%/60%/68%/76%/84%, which fall at the 12th/29th/51st/76th/92nd percentile of the national distribution.

styles/living-alone.title: Householders living alone
styles/living-alone.description: Share of households whose householder lives alone (P16), pale to deep green. Measured over all 240,563 block groups with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 18%/24%/30%/36%/44%, which fall at the 22nd/42nd/64th/80th/92nd percentile of the national distribution.

source-dhc-states.title: 2020 Census Demographic and Housing Characteristics File (DHC) — state directories
source-dhc-states.description: The 52 state archives (`{State_Name}/{ab}2020.dhc.zip`) this collection's counts were read from. Each archive holds a pipe-delimited Latin-1 geoheader plus 44 segment files joined on `LOGRECNO`; this collection reads segments carrying P16 and P17 and filters the geoheader to `SUMLEV = '150'`, `GEOCOMP = '00'`. Served by census.gov.

doc-dhc-techdoc.title: 2020 Census DHC and Demographic Profile — Technical Documentation
doc-dhc-techdoc.description: Chapter 3 (Data Dictionary) gives the table shells; Chapter 4 (Confidentiality of the Data) is the source for this collection's differential-privacy known issue. Served by census.gov.

doc-dhc-table-matrix.title: 2020 Census DHC Table Matrix
doc-dhc-table-matrix.description: Table ID, segment number and field position for every DHC table — the spreadsheet this build's field positions (tools/build_dhc.py) were derived from and verified against the real per-state files' field counts. Served by census.gov.

doc-disclosure-avoidance.title: 2020 Census Disclosure Avoidance System
doc-disclosure-avoidance.description: The Census Bureau's own explanation of the differential-privacy system that injects noise into every 2020 Census data product, this one included. Served by census.gov.

source-cartographic-boundaries.title: 2024 cartographic boundary file — census block groups (1:500,000, national)
source-cartographic-boundaries.description: The same boundary file the ACS collections at this geography join to — reused, not re-downloaded, so a DHC row and an ACS row for the same `geoid` always share the same geometry.
